name: mknodat
synopsis: int mknodat(int dirfd, const char *pathname, mode_t mode, dev_t dev);
description: The mknodat() system call creates a filesystem node (such as a file, device special file, or named pipe) with the specified mode and device number. It operates like mknod() but interprets relative pathnames relative to the directory file descriptor dirfd for better path resolution.

parameters.name: dirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor; AT_FDCWD for current working directory, otherwise ignored if pathname is absolute.

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.description: Pathname of the node to create.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: File mode and type, combined using bitwise OR (e.g., S_IFREG, S_IFCHR).

parameters.name: dev
parameters.description: Device number for special files; ignored for other file types.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: Write permission denied on the parent directory, or search permission denied in path prefix.
pathname is relative and dirfd is neither AT_FDCWD nor a valid file descriptor.
User's quota of disk blocks or inodes exhausted.
pathname already exists or is a symbolic link.
pathname points outside accessible address space.
Too many symbolic links encountered in pathname.
A directory component in pathname does not exist.
No space left on the device.
A component in pathname is not a directory.
Operation not permitted, such as creating a special file without capability.
pathname is on a read-only filesystem.

bugs: There are infelicities in the NFS protocol that may affect mknodat().
versions: Linux-specific, with mknodat introduced in Linux 2.6.16
